subject: Human Body
title: Spinal Cord Structure
description: A short lesson to help you apply Spinal Cord Structure.

hook.text: Your spinal cord is only 18 inches long and as thick as your finger. Every body signal runs through it.

buildup.text: It sits inside the vertebral column, protected by bone, membranes, and fluid, just like the brain.

discovery.text: 31 pairs of spinal nerves branch out at each vertebra. They carry signals to every part of the body below.

twist.text: The spinal cord ends at your lower back, not the tailbone. Below that, loose nerve roots dangle like a horse's tail.

climax.text: Those dangling nerves are the cauda equina. Doctors insert spinal taps here safely because the cord has already ended.

punchline.text: 18 inches of cord. Every signal your body sends uses it.

quiz.question: Where does the spinal cord actually end?
options: At the base of the neck
